and tablets, scanners, software Revenue US$ 5.40 billion (2025) Operating income US$700 million (2025) Net income US$419 million (2025) Total assets US$8.50 billion (2025) Total equity US$3.59 billion (2025) Number of employees 10,700 (2025) Website zebra .com Footnotes / references [ 1 ] Zebra Technologies Corporation (ZBR) , commonly known as Zebra , is an American multinational technology conglomerate corporation, specializing in smart data capture systems. Zebra is headquartered in Lincolnshire, Illinois . Founded in 1969, Zebra manufactures and sells marking, tracking, and computer printing technologies . Its products include mobile computers and tablets, software, thermal barcode label and receipt printers, RFID smart label printers/encoders/fixed & handheld readers/antennas, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) & machine vision (MV), and fixed industrial scanning hardware & software. and fixed industrial scanning hardware & software. [ 2 ] Zebra generated $5.4 billion in annual revenue as of 2025 and holds nearly 8,000 patents and patent applications worldwide in 2026. [ 3 ] [ 4 ] Zebra (ZBRA) stock has been listed on the NASDAQ since its initial public offering (IPO) in 1991. [ 5 ] History [ edit ] 20th century [ edit ] Zebra was incorporated in 1969 as Data Specialties Incorporated , a manufacturer of high-speed electromechanical products. [ citation needed ] The company changed its focus to specialty on-demand labeling and ticketing systems in 1982 and became Zebra Technologies Corporation in 1986. [ citation needed ] Zebra became a publicly traded company in 1991. [ citation needed ] In 1986, Zebra (then Data Specialties Incorporated) acquired Qwint Systems (formerly Martin Research), an early microcomputer pioneer which had restructured as a teletypewriter manufacturer at the beginning of the 1980s. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] In 1998, Zebra Technologies merged with Eltron

which had restructured as a teletypewriter manufacturer at the beginning of the 1980s. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] In 1998, Zebra Technologies merged with Eltron International, Inc. [ 8 ] 21st century [ edit ] In 2000, Comtec Information Systems was acquired by Zebra Technologies, [ 9 ] followed in 2003 by the acquisition of Atlantek, Inc., which was a manufacturer of photo ID printers. [ 10 ] In 2004, the company expanded into RFID smart label manufacturing. [ 11 ] [ 12 ] In the following years, Zebra also acquired Swecoin, WhereNet Corp, [ 13 ] Proveo AG, [ 14 ] and Navis Holdings (later divested in 2011). [ 15 ] The company bought the Enterprise Solutions Group (ESG) in 2008 and renamed the group Zebra Enterprise Solutions in 2009. In the same year, Multispectral Solutions, Inc. was acquired. [ 16 ] In 2012, the companies LaserBand , [ 17 ] and StepOne Systems were purchased with a cash price of $1.5 million. [ 18 ] In 2013, the company acquired Hart Systems for $94 million in cash from the

StepOne Systems were purchased with a cash price of $1.5 million. [ 18 ] In 2013, the company acquired Hart Systems for $94 million in cash from the private equity firm Topspin Partners LBO. [ 19 ] In 2014, Zebra acquired Motorola Solutions ' Enterprise Division in a $3.45 billion transaction, providing mobile computing and advanced data capture communications technologies and services. Zebra's acquisition of the Enterprise Division included the Symbol Technologies and Psion product lines. [ 19 ] [ 20 ] Also in 2014, Zebra provided its real-time location system (RTLS) in NFL stadiums to track players and officials and provide location-based data for the NFL's Next Gen Stats program. [ 21 ] [ 22 ] Zebra’s partnership with the NFL extends through the 2025 football season. [ 23 ] In 2018, the company acquired Xplore Technologies , a maker of ruggedized tablets and other hard-wearing hardware. [ 24 ] In 2019, Zebra acquired Temptime Corporation, a provider of temperature monitoring

of ruggedized tablets and other hard-wearing hardware. [ 24 ] In 2019, Zebra acquired Temptime Corporation, a provider of temperature monitoring devices to the healthcare industry. [ 25 ] That same year, Zebra also acquired Profitect, a retail software company that developed a product line used for tracking and identifying inventory losses. [ 26 ] [ 27 ] Zebra TC56 touchscreen handheld device configured in German In 2020, Zebra acquired Reflexis Systems, a provider of workforce scheduling and task management software to the retail, food service, hospitality, and banking industries [ 28 ] for $575 Million. [ 29 ] In 2021, Zebra acquired Adaptive Vision (provider of graphical Machine Vision software), Fetch Robotics (manufacturer of autonomous mobile robots) and Antuit.ai (provider of AI -powered SaaS solutions specific to forecasting and merchandising for the retail and CPG industries). [ 30 ] [ 31 ] [ 32 ] In 2022, Zebra acquired Matrox Imaging , a developer of machine vision

and merchandising for the retail and CPG industries). [ 30 ] [ 31 ] [ 32 ] In 2022, Zebra acquired Matrox Imaging , a developer of machine vision components and systems. [ 33 ] In December 2023, Zebra partnered with Verizon Business to create a software package that will allow for a faster private 5G network. Zebra tablets and computers will work on Verizon's private network, allowing for more network capacity and fast communication. [ 34 ] [ 35 ] In 2023, Zebra unveiled Zebra Workcloud - its purpose-built suite of enterprise software applications, primarily serving in retail, banking and healthcare industries. [ 36 ] Zebra also introduced the WS50 powered by Workcloud, the first wearable Android touch computer. [ 37 ] [ 38 ] References [ edit ] ^ "Zebra 2025 Annual Report" (PDF) . Zebra Technologies .
